description: Rules that report on a dotted member and go SILENT when the same member is written o['k'] — the notation bundlers and minifiers emit. SHRINK-ONLY: a rule may leave this list, never join it. Produced by scripts/find-computed-key-blind-spots.mts.
why: Extending the probe from CALLS to member READS took its reach from 282 to 349 of 470 rules and found 22 blind. Twenty-one were fixed; four of the twenty-two turned out to be artefacts of the probe itself (regex literals, and cases that deliberately contrast the two spellings), which is recorded in known_probe_artefacts. What remains is one entry that is not a defect.

known_probe_artefacts.nestjs-security/no-permissive-cors: A TYPE position: `const c: common.CorsOptions`. `common['CorsOptions']` is a valid indexed-access type, so it parses, but types are ERASED before a bundler emits anything — a subscripted type annotation cannot occur in the code this probe exists to model. Left listed rather than special-cased in the rewrite, so the judgement stays visible and reviewable.
known_probe_artefacts.browser-security/no-insecure-redirects: Removed 2026-09-02: it was never blind. The read rewrite had reached inside a REGEX literal, turning /^https:\/\/a\.example\.com/ into a["example"]. Regex literals now pass through untouched.
known_probe_artefacts.(spelling-contrast cases): Three rules left this list without a code change: react-class-to-hooks and no-direct-mutation-state were FIXED, while no-improper-type-validation was never blind — its case deliberately mixes `bag["k"]` with `bag.k`, and the rewrite normalised both, matching a guard the case exists to keep unmatched. The probe now skips a case containing both spellings of the same member.
